desc:
Amazon seller reports on sales, fees and ads turn scattered data into one clear page. Ecom Swift LLC pulls figures from your Seller Central business reports, fee statements and advertising console and explains sales, fees, returns, ad spend and what you keep.

## What is an Amazon seller report?

An Amazon seller report is a summary of how your account performed over a period. It brings together orders and units, fees charged by Amazon, returns, advertising cost and the money left over. Seller Central offers many separate reports, and each one answers only part of the question.

Our report combines them. It uses only your own account data, so nothing is estimated from outside, and each chart carries a sentence of explanation.

## Why raw data does not help on its own

Seller Central holds a lot of numbers, and most of them are hard to read together. Sales may look healthy while fees and ad spend take much of the income. A product with high traffic may convert poorly. A return reason may repeat for one item and go unnoticed because it hides in a download.

Without a clear summary, owners tend to react to the figure they happen to see: yesterday's sales, a bad review, a large ad bill. That leads to decisions made on a hunch. A regular report gives the whole picture at once.

## How reporting improves your decisions

Good reporting links cause and effect. When you see sessions and conversion by product, you can tell whether a weak item needs better images and copy or simply more traffic. When you see ad spend beside sales, you can judge which campaigns are paying their way. When you see return reasons, you can fix a sizing chart or a product detail.

The report does not change sales by itself. It tells you where to look, and each one ends with three actions to consider. Outcomes still depend on your products, prices and market.

## What a useful Amazon report includes

- Sales, units and average order value for the period.
- Amazon fees, with referral and fulfilment shown separately.
- Returns and the reasons buyers give.
- Ad spend, ACoS and what ads contributed to sales.
- Best and slowest products ranked in plain order.
- Sessions and conversion rate by product.
- A comparison to the previous period or periods.
- Product-level profit where you share your costs.
- A reusable dashboard sheet in the top package.

## How we build your report

We ask you to export or share the relevant reports: business reports, payments and fee data, and advertising data. We clean the data, match products across the sources and check that the totals agree. We then write the report in plain language, with a short note beside each chart.

You receive the report as a PDF, and in the higher packages as a spreadsheet as well. The Basic, Standard and Premium packages cover one, two and three months, with trends, a profit view and a review call added as the package grows. This is a one-off report unless you ask us to repeat it.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Share complete months so comparisons are fair.
- Provide product costs if you want a profit view.
- Tell us which questions you most want answered.
- Read the three suggested actions first.
- Keep a copy to compare with the next report.

**Avoid:**
- Judging a month by one unusually good or bad week.
- Mixing in sales from other channels without telling us.
- Ignoring returns because the rate looks small.
- Reading ad figures without checking margin.
- Making many changes at once after a single report.

## Who this is for

This service suits an owner who logs in daily but never has a clear overview. It also suits a seller preparing for a bank, investor or business partner who asks for a summary of the account. A brand that is about to hire a manager can use the report to explain where the account stands.

## What we need from you

Please send the date range, your reports or an invitation as a user with permission to view reports, and any costs you want included. We never ask for your password, and we use only the data in your own account.
